subject.title: [BUG] memory index --force CLI writes incompatible meta providerKey, breaks runtime memory_search

question: Should memory index identity mismatches from CLI/runtime providerKey or scopeHash drift stay strictly fail-closed, get an automatic rebuild/repair path, or be migrated through doctor/status recovery?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not just a mechanical lookup bug; it decides how aggressively OpenClaw protects memory index correctness versus recovering from provider/config drift for existing users.

options.title: Preserve gate, repair agreement
options.body: Keep true provider/model/scope changes fail-closed, but fix CLI/runtime identity computation and add explicit recovery proof for mismatches caused by OpenClaw's own drift.

options.title: Auto-rebuild on mismatch
options.body: Treat providerKey or scopeHash mismatch as a rebuild trigger, accepting a broader behavior change that may hide real configuration changes from users.

options.title: Defer to manual recovery
options.body: Keep current fail-closed behavior and document manual recovery only, accepting continued user-facing `memory_search` outages after some reindex workflows.

recommendation.title: Preserve gate, repair agreement
recommendation.body: Keep true provider/model/scope changes fail-closed, but fix CLI/runtime identity computation and add explicit recovery proof for mismatches caused by OpenClaw's own drift.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the memory index identity validation policy introduced in the history attributed to this contributor.
